title: Communitech partnership funding and Charles Street Terminal agreement
subtitle: Lower natural gas supply rate, faster commercial business approvals, and a regional pre-development agreement for Charles Street Terminal lands.
overview: The Finance and Corporate Services Committee spent most of its meeting on a renewed partnership with Communitech. The committee recommended that Council sign an agreement providing $500,000 a year from the Economic Development Investment Fund 2.0 for 2024 and 2025, with staff able to extend funding for 2026 and 2027 if conditions are met. Amendments added city economic development staff space inside Communitech and closer work with downtown staff. The aim is to fill vacant downtown office space.
The committee also recommended a lower natural gas supply rate for Kitchener Utilities customers from May 1, 2024, with quarterly reviews. For residents on system gas, this should lower bills.

On Charles Street Terminal, the committee recommended an agreement with the Region of Waterloo for pre-development work, with added wording on how the City's share of costs would be repaid. It also recommended using Building Enterprise funds to speed up commercial business approvals. All items go to Council for final decision. The Communitech vote was unanimous {{vote:m4}}.

decisions.detail: The committee recommended a partnership agreement with Communitech, with $500,000 each in 2024 and 2025 from the Economic Development Investment Fund 2.0 and possible staff-approved extension to 2026 and 2027.
As amended, the partnership would include office space in Communitech for city economic development staff and collaboration with downtown development staff.
The committee recommended cutting the supply component of the natural gas rate to 11.63 cents per cubic meter from 16.70, effective May 1, 2024, with quarterly reviews.
The committee recommended authorizing a Memorandum of Understanding with the Region of Waterloo for pre-development work, with the Region carrying costs and the City reimbursing its share.
The City's share would come from land sale proceeds if its lands are sold, or from an alternate source such as the Economic Development Reserve if not.

The committee recommended using Building Enterprise funds for an 18-month project manager secondment and early improvements, and reallocating remaining Development Services Review capital funds to the project.

debate: Staff said the partnership responds to high downtown office vacancy and a thinner pipeline of scaling companies since the pandemic, and that funding would shift to specific on-site programs with measured results.
Communitech and a delegate who supports it argued that city funding helps it attract senior-government and private funding and that in-person space gives startups connection that remote work lacks.

Councillors raised concerns about accountability and recognition: one asked for annual reporting, and staff agreed to provide a standalone annual update without a motion. Others asked for tracking of companies that move into downtown offices.

One councillor noted that other municipalities in the region contribute little to Communitech and should be encouraged to invest. Another asked whether other incubators might seek similar funding, and staff said any request would face the same review.
On Charles Street Terminal, the amendment's mover said it clarifies that the City's lands have not been approved for sale. Staff said it matches the report's intent.
